correctness.rationale: For B=(x-y)(x+y)(x²+y²-z²)(2y²-z²)(2x²-z²), the square-coordinate quotient (X,Y,Z)=(x²,y²,z²) sends all four component-orbit equations to four lines concurrent at [1:1:2]. A smooth diagonal conic with abc≠0 is a quotient line L=(a,b,c); when F=a+b+2c≠0, L meets the four lines at distinct points. Cross products give exactly six branch forms a+b,a-b,a+c,b+c,a+2c,b+2c; each simple coordinate-branch event replaces four lifts with two, yielding k=16-2r. Exact independent cross-product/parameter-line arithmetic reproduces the sole admissible r=3 point [2:2:-1] and the six r=2 points. When F=0, the conic joins the existing pencil with four transverse local basepoints and k=4. At generic r>0, a nonzero square restriction gives simple A3 tangency; the F=0 ordinary five-branch points are locally homogeneous, so the required triples are quasihomogeneous. The exact Măcinic Theorem 3.7 and resolution Corollary 3.17 for base exponents (2,5) then give free exponents (2,7) on F=0, free (4,5) at r=3, plus-one (4,6) level 7 at r=2, neither at r=1,0 with the stated graded resolutions. This proves only the smooth diagonal family, not arbitrary conics; finite incidence verification does not prove the external addition theorem.
